column1: #! schema = 1
# THE PERFORMANCE GATE. Compared for EQUALITY, not within a tolerance.
# Allocations for parse+serialize over the committed golden cases. These numbers
# are exact: identical across runs, across platforms, and across optimisation
# levels (verified in both debug and release). There is no noise to tolerate.
# Why this and not timings: benches/baselines/linux-x86_64.tsv was calibrated
# from a CI run on `main`, and the next run flagged a 43% regression on a parser
# that had not changed by a byte. Six runs showed criterion measuring to within
# ±1% inside a run while the same benchmark moved +38%/-20% between runs — and
# the failing run was the FASTEST of six for three benchmarks and the slowest for
# a fourth, so it was not simply a slow host. See ADR-006's second amendment.
# Fewer allocations is an improvement: record the new numbers. More is a
# regression: explain it, then record them. Either way it is a reviewed change
# (§8), and golden-guard covers this path.
# yaml 3130 -> 3132 on 2026-08-09: the entire structural validation pass costs
# two allocations across 37 golden cases, both the field split in
# `check_yaml_directive` for case 260's two directive lines. The first draft cost
# 290 — a Vec per line and another for the whole token stream — and this gate is
# what surfaced that.
# yaml 3132 -> 3134 on 2026-08-09: flow-context validation. Two allocations
# across 37 golden cases, and they are the two cases that actually contain a
# flow collection — `Vec::new()` does not allocate until something is pushed, so
# a document with no `[` or `{` pays nothing at all. JSON is unchanged at 2261,
# which is the check: these rules are YAML-only and a JSON movement would have
# meant one had leaked.
# Not avoidable by being cleverer. Tracking bracket nesting needs a stack, and a
# fixed-size array would trade an allocation for a depth limit on valid input —
# the wrong direction, since refusing a deeply-nested valid document is the
# error this parser keeps deciding not to make.
# format
json
yaml
